title: Perf-Canary Alert Tuning Notes (SRE) — backtesting + thresholds + dedup rules
content:
Doc purpose
- Capture SRE alert tuning decisions for perf-regression canary (prod) based on backtesting and early rollout signals.
- Focus: paging hygiene, detector thresholds, minimum sample sizing, and dedup/grouping rules.

Owners
- Primary: Sean Gallagher (SRE lead)
- PagerDuty + routing integration: Rafael Mendes
- Paging hygiene/runbook review: Tomáš Novák
- Telemetry/metric semantics review: Logan Wright + Nadia Rahman

Scope (v1)
- Signals: p95 latency and tokens/sec (TPS) per model + region + GPU SKU slice.
- Baseline: rolling median (7d) with deploy-window suppression (see ADR-0231).
- Canary traffic: source=perf-canary only; do NOT page on customer traffic directly (customer impact handled via separate SLO alerts).

Data sets used for backtesting
- Time range: 2026-01-10 → 2026-02-06 (28 days)
- Regions: us-east (primary), eu-west (partial coverage)
- Models in canary set during this window:
  - llama-3.1-70b-instruct (streaming + non-streaming)
  - qwen2.5-72b-instruct (streaming + non-streaming)
  - mistral-large (non-streaming)
- GPU SKUs observed: A100-80G, H100-80G (note: some short-lived mixed pools in us-east during capacity moves)

Methodology
- Replay aggregated time-series at 1m resolution.
- Detector: regression vs baseline (rolling 7d median), with minimum samples and outlier trimming already applied upstream (Telemetry doc: perf-canary-metrics-validation, plus ENG-2845/ENG-2852 work).
- Suppress during deploy windows and known warmup windows (see “Suppressions” section).
- Evaluate alert volume and “page-worthiness” by triage time and actionability.

Summary of backtesting results (before tuning)
- With naive thresholds (p95 +10% for 10m; TPS -10% for 10m) we would have paged ~6.1 times/day in us-east alone.
- Root causes of false positives:
  1) Deploy annotations arriving late / misaligned with aggregation windows (fixed by PR 39249 but still need suppression buffer)
  2) Canary runner restarts (warm caches, JIT/autotune drift, cold KV) → transient p95 spikes
  3) GPU SKU mixing (A100 + H100) combined into one series → apparent “regression” when fleet composition shifts
  4) Streaming TPS bug early on (fixed by PR 39157) generated repeated TPS “drops” on streaming panels
  5) Short-term node contention (single node noisy neighbors) causing p95 spikes without sustained shift in median

After tuning (proposed in this doc)
- Expected page volume during stable periods: ~0.3–0.6 pages/day across both regions, with most pages tied to deploys or real fleet events.
- Ticket volume (non-page) expected: ~1.0–1.8/day (mostly “watch” regressions or borderline shifts).

Proposed alert thresholds (v1)

A) p95 latency regression (paging)
- Condition:
  - p95_latency_ms / baseline_p95_latency_ms >= 1.18 (>= +18%)
  - For >= 20 minutes (sustained)
  - Minimum sample size: >= 250 requests in the evaluation window per series
  - Only evaluate when baseline is “healthy”: baseline_p95_latency_ms computed from >= 3 of last 7 days meeting sample min
- Page severity: SEV3 page to SRE oncall (perf-canary service)
- Rationale:
  - +15% caught too many warmup and mixed-SKU artifacts; +18% materially reduces noise while still catching kernel/scheduler regressions we’ve seen in staging.

B) p95 latency regression (ticket-only)
- Condition:
  - p95_latency_ms / baseline_p95_latency_ms >= 1.12 (>= +12%)
  - For >= 30 minutes
  - Minimum sample size: >= 400 requests (stricter since it’s slower-moving)
- Action: create ticket in Runtime queue, label “perf-canary-watch”; no page.
- Purpose: early signal / trend, but not urgent.

C) tokens/sec regression (paging)
- Condition:
  - tokens_per_sec / baseline_tokens_per_sec <= 0.86 (<= -14%)
  - For >= 25 minutes
  - Minimum sample size: >= 150 requests
  - Only for non-streaming + streaming separately (do not combine)
- Page severity: SEV3 page
- Notes:
  - TPS is more variance-sensitive than p95 in our replays; longer duration reduces noise.

D) tokens/sec regression (ticket-only)
- Condition:
  - tokens_per_sec / baseline_tokens_per_sec <= 0.92 (<= -8%)
  - For >= 45 minutes
  - Minimum sample size: >= 250
- Action: ticket-only.

E) Guardrail: “data health” / canary misbehavior (paging)
- Condition (any):
  - Missing required labels (model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build) above 5% of canary traffic for 15m
  - Canary request error rate > 2% for 10m (5xx from runtime)
- Page severity: SEV3 page
- Rationale: if canary is blind or broken, we lose detection. This should be rare.

Alert evaluation windows / aggregation notes
- Evaluate on 1m buckets but require sustained duration as above.
- For p95, we rely on upstream quantile aggregation correctness. We need strict alignment between runtime-emitted histograms and telemetry windows (PR 39249 addressed a mismatch; keep a validation check in place).

Suppressions / maintenance windows (to reduce false positives)

1) Deploy-window suppression
- Suppress regression alerts for a series when a runtime deploy annotation is observed for that (region, gpu_sku) slice.
- Window:
  - start: deploy annotation timestamp - 10 minutes
  - end: deploy annotation timestamp + 35 minutes
- Why:
  - We see “deploy smear” due to staggered rollout + warmup + cache effects.
  - Annotation arrival can lag by a few minutes; negative buffer avoids firing right before annotation appears.

2) Canary runner restart suppression
- Suppress for 12 minutes after canary runner restart per region.
- Trigger: canary runner emits heartbeat metric with instance_id; on change, suppress.
- Why:
  - Cold prefix/KV cache, JIT kernel selection warmup, and early batching behavior are unstable.

3) GPU SKU rebalancing / capacity moves
- If gpu_sku label is missing or “unknown”, DO NOT evaluate regression alerts; instead fire a ticket-only “label health” warning.
- If a series shows gpu_sku share change > 25% within 30m (heuristic), suppress paging and file ticket-only “fleet composition shift” note.
- Why:
  - Mixed SKU is the single biggest source of non-actionable noise in backtests.

4) Planned maintenance
- Use standard SRE maintenance window tooling (via slo-toolkit helper, PR 410) to suppress pages.
- Requirement: maintenance window must include region and approximate time; optionally include runtime_version.

False positives we saw (examples)

FP1: p95 spike during deploy due to annotation lag
- Date: 2026-01-19
- Symptom: llama-3.1-70b-instruct us-east H100 p95 up ~22% for ~12m
- Root cause: runtime deploy started ~5m before annotation showed up; detector fired during the gap.
- Fix: deploy suppression window now includes -10m buffer; plus PR 39249 for alignment.

FP2: streaming TPS “regression” (pre-fix)
- Date: 2026-01-16 → 2026-01-17
- Symptom: qwen2.5-72b-instruct streaming TPS down ~15–25% in several bursts
- Root cause: TPS calculation bug for streaming (timestamp alignment); fixed in PR 39157.
- Action: backtest excludes pre-fix period for TPS threshold calibration; keep stricter duration on TPS paging.

FP3: GPU pool mix created apparent regression
- Date: 2026-01-24
- Symptom: mistral-large us-east combined series p95 up ~18% while TPS down ~10%
- Root cause: A100 instances introduced temporarily; without gpu_sku slice this looked like regression.
- Action: enforce gpu_sku as required label; no evaluation on unknown/mixed.

FP4: Canary runner restart + cold caches
- Date: 2026-01-29
- Symptom: p95 up ~30% for 8–10m, then normal
- Root cause: canary runner restarted during node drain; cold path + low batching.
- Fix: 12m post-restart suppression.

FP5: node contention outlier
- Date: 2026-02-02
- Symptom: one short p95 spike (3–4 minutes) in eu-west
- Root cause: suspected single node noisy neighbor; not sustained.
- Fix: sustained duration requirement (20m) and min sample gates.

Proposed dedup + grouping rules (Alertmanager/PagerDuty)

Goals
- One page per actionable “regression event”, not per panel.
- Avoid paged storms from correlated metrics (p95 + TPS both moving) and correlated slices (same runtime_build across multiple models).

Definitions
- “Series key” labels (must be present):
  - model
  - region
  - gpu_sku
  - traffic_mode (streaming | non_streaming)
  - metric (p95_latency_ms | tokens_per_sec)
- “Attribution” labels (for context, not grouping):
  - runtime_build (or runtime_version + git_sha)
  - scheduler_mode
  - kernel_id

Grouping (PagerDuty incident grouping key)
- Proposed grouping key:
  - region + gpu_sku + runtime_build + metric
- Why:
  - If one runtime_build is bad in a slice, we want one incident per metric type to coordinate rollback/mitigation.
  - We do NOT want separate incidents for each model if they all regress together after a deploy (common case).

Dedup rules (within an incident)
- Dedup if:
  - Same (region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, metric) regardless of model, as long as models are within the canary set.
- Payload must include:
  - Top impacted models (up to 5) sorted by regression magnitude
  - Links to per-model dashboards for those models

Splitting rules (create separate incidents)
- Split if:
  - Different runtime_build (since rollback candidates differ)
  - Different gpu_sku (since kernel path differs)
  - Different region (operationally independent)

Noise control rules
- If both p95 and TPS regress concurrently, page on p95 first; TPS alert should auto-silence if a p95 page is already open for same (region, gpu_sku, runtime_build) within last 60m.
- Rationale: responders can treat TPS drop as supporting evidence; don’t double-page.

Alert payload requirements (must-have fields)
- Regression magnitude vs baseline (ratio + absolute)
- Baseline definition (rolling 7d median) + number of baseline days contributing
- Sample size + request rate
- Runtime build + git SHA
- Scheduler mode + pinned config flags (if any)
- GPU SKU
- Dashboard links:
  - Overview heatmap
  - Model detail (top impacted models)
  - Deploy annotation view
- Runbook link: Runbook: perf-canary regression triage

Proposed severity mapping
- SEV3 Page (PagerDuty): sustained regression crossing paging threshold AND not suppressed.
- Ticket-only:
  - Watch thresholds
  - Label/metrics health issues
  - Fleet composition shift heuristic triggered

Operational notes / runbook alignment
- First responder: SRE oncall validates signal quality + suppression correctness.
- Escalation: if confirmed not noise and correlates to runtime_build, assign Runtime oncall (Serving Runtime: Kernel/Scheduling) and keep SRE as incident commander for comms.
- If regression correlates to a single runtime build and started within the last deploy window, preferred mitigation is rollback (per release train guidance) unless Runtime can quickly pinpoint a safe flag/config mitigation.

Open questions / TODOs
- Confirm whether we want to incorporate a “known-good pinned build” baseline for top-tier models (hybrid baseline). ADR leans rolling median, but for very frequent deploys rolling baseline can drift.
- Validate thresholds per model family: some models have higher natural TPS variance under streaming.
- Add automated “did gpu_sku mix change?” panel and include in alert payload.
- Ensure dashboard annotations include both runtime deploys and canary runner deploys/restarts.

Decision log (so far)
- 2026-02-05: Agree to longer sustained duration for TPS paging (25m) due to variance.
- 2026-02-07: Adopt grouping key at (region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, metric) to avoid multi-model page storms.
- 2026-02-10: Add -10m buffer to deploy suppression to handle annotation delays.

Appendix: quick reference thresholds
- p95 paging: +18% for 20m, min 250 req
- p95 ticket: +12% for 30m, min 400 req
- TPS paging: -14% for 25m, min 150 req
- TPS ticket: -8% for 45m, min 250 req
- Canary restart suppression: 12m
- Deploy suppression: -10m → +35m

Contact
- #eng-sre for tuning changes
- #eng-runtime for confirmed regressions
- File follow-up tasks under ENG-2846 (detector) / ENG-2848 (routing) / ENG-2855 (backtesting)
